subject: Unit-econ checkpoints & evaluation timeline for Medicore MAP
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@medicore.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@medicore.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: MAP ask — unit econ checks + evaluation plan

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Medicore's clinical search pilot team is excited to run an evaluation. Procurement asked me to get a concrete Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes the evaluation timeline, acceptance criteria, and the cost assumptions (tokens/$, caching, batching).

Can you share: 
- A short evaluation plan (3–4 week pilot) with clear success metrics we can include in the MAP
- A unit-econ sensitivity table (tokens per API call, expected caching delta, batching assumptions) so finance can sanity-check pricing
- Any operational constraints or SLOs that would affect the economics (max latency for interactive search, TTL for cached prefixes)

We need something to attach to the internal procurement review by Friday 4/5.

Appreciate it — feel free to loop in whoever on your side.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Digital Clinical Search
Medicore Health

Attachment: Medicore_RFP_summary.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@medicore.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial: MAP ask — unit econ checks + evaluation plan

Hi Alyssa — thanks, this is great context. Attaching a draft MAP and a preliminary unit-econ workbook (see attachments). High level answers below; Ill put the detailed numbers in the spreadsheet and Drive link.

Quick summary (pilot = 3 weeks):
- Evaluation scope: 10k daily search queries, mix of short queries (avg 120 tokens total output) and long context retrieval (avg 450 tokens).
- Success metrics: 95th %-tile latency < 350ms for interactive flows; relevance uplift (MAP-specific NDCG) >= 12% over baseline; error rate < 0.5%.

Unit-econ baseline assumptions (conservative):
- Per-response generation: 1.2k tokens consumed on average (prompt + response), split: prompt ~600, response ~600.
- Cost per token (hosted): model tier estimate $0.000012 / token (example) -> baseline cost per call ~$0.0144.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache expected to reduce average per-call tokens by ~28% for common queries; prefetching hot prefixes lowers prompt tokens by up to 45% in steady state.
- Batching: for batch inference (non-interactive bulk eval) we expect up to 2.5x throughput with negligible quality delta; effective tokens/$ improves ~30% in batched runs.

Immediate ask for Medicore procurement packet: can we confirm target daily query profile (short vs long %) and whether the evaluation will allow a 48–72 hour batched re-run window? That determines whether we model batched vs interactive economics.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal: we finalize the spreadsheet and MAP doc by EOD 4/2.
2) Review: 4/3 internal alignment call (Redwood + Medicore) to lock acceptance criteria.
3) Sign: we prepare a short SOW and DocuSign envelope for pilot start 4/8.

Attachments: medicore_map_draft_v2.pdf, unit_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx

Thanks — looping Tessa and Neha to validate the caching/batching numbers.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial: MAP ask — unit econ checks + evaluation plan

On Mon, Apr 1, 2029 at 11:08 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick summary (pilot = 3 weeks):
> - Evaluation scope: 10k daily search queries...

Adding operational details from infra that matter for the numbers: 
- Cache hit assumptions: For clinical search with a well-curated prefix set, we should model a 25–35% steady-state prefix hit rate in week 2–3; early-stage (week 1) will be lower (~10–15%).
- Prefetching: If Medicore can provide a top-1k queries log, our prefetch engine can reduce prompt tokens for that tail by ~40% with a small warm-up cost.
- KV cache retention: default TTL 15 minutes for session-scoped caches. Increasing to 2 hours helps sustained clinical flows but increases memory; SRE recommends starting with 30m and adjusting.
- Batching notes: For the evaluation, if Medicore agrees to a nightly batched rerun for analytics (vs strict day-of-interactive accuracy), we can model a conservative 25% tokens/$ improvement in the evaluation cost column; aggressive batching with 4k batch size could reach ~35% improvement but may change sampling characteristics.

I updated the spreadsheet (column: week1/week2/week3 with token estimates). Key ask for Alyssa: share estimated daily short/long query split and whether nightly batched reruns are acceptable for the analytics portion of the pilot.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized MAP + pilot timeline and SOW link

Alyssa / Medicore procurement team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Attached is the revised MAP (medicore_map_draft_v2.pdf) and the unit economics workbook (unit_econ_spreadsheet.xlsx). Summary of changes since draft:
- We included week-by-week token burn profiles (week1 warm-up, week2 steady-state, week3 optimized with prefetch).
- Modeled two scenarios in the workbook: interactive-only (no batching) and mixed-mode (nightly batched analytics + interactive day traffic). Mixed-mode shows ~22–28% lower cost per accepted evaluation due to batching and caching combined.
- SLOs: 95th%-tile latency target remains 350ms for interactive; batched runs have no latency SLO but have a 72-hour window for completion.

Proposed timeline: 
- 4/4: Medicore confirms query profile and approves MAP content
- 4/5: Procurement internal review complete
- 4/6: Redwood sends DocuSign for a 3-week pilot SOW
- 4/8: Pilot starts (data ingest + warm-up)

Action items for Medicore (please confirm by EOD 4/4):
1) Short vs long query split estimate (approx %).
2) Approval for nightly batched reruns for analytics (yes/no).
3) Signature on SOW once DocuSign arrives.
